evidence.description: The `updateTrackerController` method directly modifies the `shared` instance's `tracker` property, which is a private property of the singleton.

candidates.explanation: Modifying a singleton's internal state via a static method can lead to side effects and makes the state harder to reason about, especially if multiple parts of the app trigger updates simultaneously.
candidates.title: Singleton State Mutation via Static Method

evidence.description: The `endpoint` variable is force-unwrapped when initializing `NetworkConfiguration`.

candidates.explanation: Force-unwrapping a value obtained from a provider (`urlProvider.snowplowMicro` or `urlProvider.snowplow`) can lead to a runtime crash if the provider returns nil.
candidates.title: Force Unwrapping of Optional Value

evidence.description: The `shouldUseMicroInstance` property setter calls `Analytics.updateTrackerController()`, which re-instantiates the tracker.

candidates.explanation: The setter for `shouldUseMicroInstance` triggers a side effect that replaces the tracker instance. If this property is updated frequently or during sensitive operations, it could lead to lost events or inconsistent tracking state.
candidates.title: Side Effect in Property Setter

evidence.description: The `track` method returns early if `User.shared.sendAnonymousUsageData` is false, but it does not provide any mechanism to handle the case where data should be sent but the flag is unexpectedly false.

candidates.explanation: While this might be intended behavior, relying on a global shared state (`User.shared`) to gate all tracking events can make debugging missing data difficult as the logic is centralized and opaque.
candidates.title: Silent Failure on Condition Check
